clinicalPearls: A telomere biology disorder caused by variants in telomere maintenance genes (e.g. DKC1, TERT, TERC, TINF2), with X-linked, autosomal dominant, and recessive forms
Classic mucocutaneous triad: reticulate skin hyperpigmentation, nail dystrophy, and oral leukoplakia
Bone marrow failure is the leading cause of early mortality and may present as cytopenias or aplastic anaemia
Markedly increased risk of myelodysplasia, leukaemia, and mucosal squamous cell carcinomas
Pulmonary fibrosis and hepatic disease are important non-haematological complications
The severe infantile variant Hoyeraal-Hreidarsson syndrome adds cerebellar hypoplasia and immunodeficiency
Very short telomeres for age (measured by flow-FISH) strongly support the diagnosis alongside gene testing
reference.pathophysiology: Dyskeratosis congenita is caused by defects in the telomere maintenance machinery, including the telomerase enzyme complex and shelterin proteins that protect chromosome ends. Inadequate telomere maintenance leads to accelerated telomere shortening, so highly proliferative tissues such as bone marrow, skin, mucosa, and lung exhaust their replicative capacity prematurely. Cells undergo senescence or apoptosis, producing the progressive stem-cell failure that underlies bone marrow failure, mucocutaneous changes, and organ fibrosis. Genomic instability from dysfunctional telomeres also explains the heightened predisposition to haematological and epithelial malignancies.
additionalDifferentials: Fanconi anaemia and other inherited bone marrow failure syndromes
Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis of other cause
additionalInvestigations: Telomere length measurement by flow-FISH in leucocyte subsets
Molecular genetic testing of telomere biology disorder genes
Full blood count and bone marrow examination for cytopenias and marrow failure
Pulmonary function tests and imaging for interstitial lung disease
Liver function and imaging for hepatic involvement
Surveillance examination of oral and mucosal surfaces for premalignant change
redFlags: Progressive pancytopenia or evolving bone marrow failure
Features of myelodysplasia or acute leukaemia
Non-healing or indurated oral leukoplakia suggesting squamous carcinoma
reference.prognosis: Prognosis is guarded and shortened, dominated by bone marrow failure, malignancy, and pulmonary or hepatic fibrosis; haematopoietic stem cell transplantation can address marrow failure but does not remove the ongoing cancer and organ-fibrosis risks, so lifelong surveillance is essential.
pitfalls: Treating apparent acquired aplastic anaemia without recognising an underlying telomere disorder, which alters transplant conditioning
Using standard-intensity chemotherapy or radiotherapy that is poorly tolerated in these patients
Overlooking pulmonary and hepatic complications by focusing only on skin and marrow
Failing to screen at-risk relatives given variable inheritance and anticipation
references: Nathan and Oski's Hematology and Oncology of Infancy and Childhood
